info.name: ERP-Cafe — Inventory API (v1)
info.description:
Every endpoint of the ERP-Cafe inventory module: ingredients, items (supplier ↔ ingredient purchase mapping), suppliers, stock and purchase orders.

## Getting started
1. Select the **ERP-Cafe — Local** environment.
2. Run **00 · Setup → Login** — it stores `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `companyId` and the first accessible `branchId` into the environment.
3. Every other request inherits Bearer auth from the collection; branch-scoped ones send `X-Branch-Id: {{branchId}}`.

## Conventions
- Base path `/api/v1`; `baseUrl` defaults to `http://localhost:8090` (dev profile).
- Create requests capture the new id (and `version`) into environment variables, so the whole collection can be run top-to-bottom in the Collection Runner and pass green — the delete requests target scratch rows on purpose, and the purchase order is only partially received so it can still be cancelled.
- Ingredients / items / suppliers use optimistic locking: PUT echoes the `version` you loaded. A stale value returns 409; omitting it skips the check.
- Branch-scoped endpoints (stock, purchase orders) return 422 "Active branch required" without `X-Branch-Id`.
- Errors are RFC 7807 ProblemDetail: 400 validation, 404 not found, 409 conflict/stale version, 422 business rule.
- Units: `mg, g, kg, ml, cl, l, pc` — an item's `unit` must measure the same dimension as its ingredient's `baseUnit`.

exec: // Surface the ProblemDetail message whenever a request fails — saves opening the body tab.

item.name: 00 · Setup
item.description: Authenticate and pick up the ids the rest of the collection needs.

request.description: Exchanges credentials for a 15-minute access token and a 30-day refresh token. Stores both in the environment.

exec: console.warn('This user has no branch access — stock and purchase-order calls will 403/422.');

request.description: Identity of the bearer: userId, email, companyId, accessible branchIds, roles and permissions. Run this before the branch-scoped folders — it fills `branchId`.
Optional alternative to `/auth/me` for picking a branch. Requires the `branch:read` permission.
Rotates the token pair when the 15-minute access token expires.

item.name: 01 · Ingredients
item.description: Company-scoped master data — what the café counts stock in. Permissions: `inventory:read` / `inventory:write`.

request.description:
GET /api/v1/ingredients — every ingredient of the caller's company (unpaged).

200 → `IngredientResponse[]`: `{ id, companyId, name, baseUnit, category, active, version }`

exec: pm.test('Location header points at the new row', () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get('Location')).to.include(body.id));

request.description:
POST /api/v1/ingredients

Body: `name`* (≤255), `baseUnit`* (≤16 — one of `mg, g, kg, ml, cl, l, pc`), `category` (≤64), `active` (defaults true). `version` is ignored on create.

201 → `IngredientResponse` + `Location`. A duplicate name in the same company → **409**.

GET /api/v1/ingredients/{id} — tenant-scoped: an id belonging to another company returns **404**, not the row.

Refreshes `ingredientVersion` for the next update.

PUT /api/v1/ingredients/{id} — full replace.

`version` is the stale-form guard: echo the value you loaded and a concurrent edit is rejected with **409** instead of being overwritten. Drop the field to skip the check.

exec: pm.test('409 Conflict on a stale form', () => pm.response.to.have.status(409));

request.description: Demonstrates the optimistic lock: a version that no longer matches the row returns **409** "Ingredient was modified by someone else — reload and try again".

exec: // Creates a throwaway ingredient and deletes that one, so a top-to-bottom
// collection run keeps {{ingredientId}} alive for the Items / Stock / PO folders.
// To delete the ingredient you actually created, point the URL at {{ingredientId}}.
raw: JSON.stringify({ name: 'Scratch ingredient ' + Date.now(), baseUnit: 'g', category: 'Scratch' })
console.warn('Scratch ingredient not created — falling back to {{ingredientId}}');

request.description:
DELETE /api/v1/ingredients/{id} → **204**. Hard delete — prefer `active: false` for anything with stock history.

The pre-request script spins up a scratch ingredient and deletes that, so running the whole collection doesn't pull the rug out from under the Items / Stock / Purchase Order folders. Swap the URL to `{{ingredientId}}` to delete the one you created above.

item.name: 02 · Suppliers
item.description: Who the café buys from. Permissions: `inventory:read` / `inventory:write`.

request.description: GET /api/v1/suppliers → `SupplierResponse[]`: `{ id, companyId, name, contactPhone, contactEmail, address, active, version }`

body.raw:
{
  "name": "Highland Coffee Roasters",
  "contactPhone": "0901234567",
  "contactEmail": "sales@highland.example",
  "address": "12 Nguyen Hue, District 1, HCMC",
  "active": true
}

request.description:
POST /api/v1/suppliers

Body: `name`* (≤255), `contactPhone` (≤32), `contactEmail` (valid email), `address` (≤500), `active`.

Duplicate name in the company → **409**.
GET /api/v1/suppliers/{id} — tenant-scoped, cross-company id → **404**.
PUT /api/v1/suppliers/{id} — full replace, with the same `version` stale-edit guard as ingredients (**409** on mismatch).

exec: // Same trick as Delete ingredient: delete a scratch row so {{supplierId}} survives
// for the Items and Purchase Order folders. Point the URL at {{supplierId}} to
// delete the supplier created above instead.
console.warn('Scratch supplier not created — falling back to {{supplierId}}');

request.description:
DELETE /api/v1/suppliers/{id} → **204**.

Deletes a scratch supplier created by the pre-request script so a full collection run keeps `{{supplierId}}` usable; switch the URL to `{{supplierId}}` to delete the real one.

item.name: 03 · Items
item.description:
The buy-side catalogue: one supplier's product for one ingredient, in the unit it is sold by. Permissions: `inventory:read` / `inventory:write`.

Run **01 · Create ingredient** and **02 · Create supplier** first — these requests reuse `{{ingredientId}}` and `{{supplierId}}`.

query.description: Optional — narrow to one supplier's catalogue (what a PO may draw from).
Optional — every way this ingredient can be bought.

request.description:
GET /api/v1/items — both query params are optional and combinable.

200 → `ItemResponse[]`: `{ id, companyId, sku, name, supplierId, ingredientId, unit, active, version }`

POST /api/v1/items

Body: `sku` (≤64, optional — suppliers without codes aren't forced to invent one), `name`* (≤255), `supplierId`*, `ingredientId`*, `unit`* (≤16), `active`.

Rules:
- `unit` must share a dimension with the ingredient's `baseUnit` — kg against g is fine, kg against ml → **422**.
- Same SKU twice for one supplier → **409**.
- Same supplier + ingredient + unit twice → **409**.
- Unknown `supplierId` / `ingredientId` (or one from another company) → **404**.
Buying a gram-counted ingredient by the litre is a mapping error, not a rounding one — rejected at create time with **422** "Cannot buy X in l: X is counted in g".
GET /api/v1/items/{id} — tenant-scoped, cross-company id → **404**.

PUT /api/v1/items/{id} — updates `sku`, `name`, `unit`, `active`.

`supplierId` and `ingredientId` are **fixed at create and ignored here**: an item is one supplier's product for one ingredient, and repointing it would rewrite what past purchases meant. Send them anyway (they're `@NotNull` on the DTO) or validation fails with 400.

Stale `version` → **409**.
DELETE /api/v1/items/{id} → **204**.

item.name: 04 · Stock
item.description: On-hand levels and the movement ledger for the **active branch**. Every request sends `X-Branch-Id: {{branchId}}` — without it the API answers **422** "Active branch required". Permissions: `inventory:read` / `inventory:write`.

request.description:
GET /api/v1/stock → `StockItemResponse[]`:
`{ ingredientId, branchId, quantityOnHand, reorderLevel, avgUnitCost: { amount, currency }, belowReorderLevel }`

Quantities are in the ingredient's `baseUnit`; `avgUnitCost` is the moving-average cost.
GET /api/v1/stock/low — only the rows at or under their reorder level; the reorder alert feed.

GET /api/v1/stock/movements — paged append-only ledger.

200 → `PageResponse<MovementResponse>`: `{ content[], page, size, totalElements, totalPages }` where each entry is `{ id, ingredientId, branchId, type, quantity, unitCost, refType, refId, note, occurredAt, actor }`.

`type` covers purchase receipts, sales deduction, adjustments and waste.

POST /api/v1/stock/adjust — signed correction against a stocktake.

Body: `ingredientId`*, `quantityDelta`* (in the ingredient's base unit; **negative to write stock down**), `note`.

200 → the updated `StockItemResponse`. Ingredient from another company → **422**.

POST /api/v1/stock/waste — writes stock off as loss, kept separate from adjustments so waste stays reportable.

Body: `ingredientId`*, `quantity`* (**positive** — the amount lost), `note`. Zero or negative → **422**.

PUT /api/v1/stock/reorder-level — the threshold that puts an ingredient on the low-stock list for this branch.

Body: `ingredientId`*, `reorderLevel`* (≥ 0, base unit).

item.name: 05 · Purchase Orders
item.description:
Buying for the **active branch** (`X-Branch-Id` required). Lifecycle: create (DRAFT) → send (SENT) → receive (partial or full) / cancel. Receiving is what moves stock and updates moving-average cost.

Permissions: **`purchasing:read` / `purchasing:write`** — these differ from the rest of the module.

request.description: GET /api/v1/purchase-orders → `PageResponse<PurchaseOrderResponse>` for the active branch.

POST /api/v1/purchase-orders

Body: `supplierId`*, `note`, `lines`* (non-empty) of `{ ingredientId*, orderedQty* > 0, unitCost* ≥ 0 }`.

`orderedQty` and `unitCost` are in the ingredient's base unit. Empty `lines` → **422**; supplier or ingredient from another company → **422**.

201 → `PurchaseOrderResponse` `{ id, branchId, supplierId, status, note, lines[{ id, ingredientId, orderedQty, receivedQty, unitCost{amount,currency} }] }`. Captures `purchaseOrderId` and `poLineId`.
GET /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id} — order with its lines, including `receivedQty` so far.
POST /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}/send — no body. DRAFT → SENT; the order is now receivable and its lines are frozen.

POST /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}/receive — books the delivery: raises stock, writes ledger movements and rolls the moving-average cost.

Body: `receipts`* (non-empty) of `{ lineId*, receivedQty* > 0, unitCostOverride? }`. Use `unitCostOverride` when the invoice price differs from the ordered price; omit or `null` to keep the line's cost.

Accepted in status `SENT` **or** `PARTIALLY_RECEIVED` — partial deliveries are normal: send a smaller `receivedQty` and call again for the rest. Status becomes `PARTIALLY_RECEIVED` until every line is complete, then `RECEIVED`.

This example deliberately receives 3000 of the 5000 ordered so the order stays `PARTIALLY_RECEIVED` and the **Cancel** request below still works in a straight top-to-bottom run. Raise it to 5000 to close the order.

**422** when: the order is `DRAFT`/`RECEIVED`/`CANCELLED`, `receivedQty` ≤ 0, or the quantity exceeds what's still outstanding. Unknown `lineId` → **404**.
Receiving more than the outstanding quantity is refused with **422** "Received quantity exceeds outstanding for line …".

POST /api/v1/purchase-orders/{id}/cancel — no body. Closes an order that will not be delivered; already-received stock stays booked.

Allowed from `DRAFT`, `SENT` and `PARTIALLY_RECEIVED`. A fully `RECEIVED` or already `CANCELLED` order → **422** "Cannot cancel a RECEIVED order".

item.name: 06 · Negative checks
item.description: Quick probes for the cross-cutting behaviour: auth, tenant scoping and the branch header.

request.description: Every inventory endpoint needs a bearer token.

Branch-scoped writes without the header → **422** "Active branch required (set X-Branch-Id header)".

The JWT filter handles the other two cases before the controller is reached: a non-UUID header → **400** "Malformed X-Branch-Id", a branch outside the user's accessible set → **403** "No access to branch …".
Also the response for an id that exists but belongs to another company — the by-id endpoints are tenant-scoped, so they never confirm a foreign row exists.
Bean-validation failures come back as **400** "Validation failed" with the offending fields listed.
